# pbidriver

> pbidriver is an open-source (MIT) Python command-line tool and MCP server, "WebDriver for Power BI Desktop", that
> lets AI agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex and Cursor build, see and drive Microsoft Power BI
> Desktop reports on Windows: create PBIP projects, pages and visuals; pixel-exact screenshots of report pages,
> single visuals and the Table, Model, DAX query and TMDL views; the data behind visuals; blocking dialogs; slicers,
> clicks, tooltips, menus, scrolling and bookmarks; refresh, DAX queries and model metadata; and Performance Analyzer
> timings. With Microsoft's Power BI Modeling MCP (which edits the semantic model) it is a complete kit for agents to
> build Power BI reports end to end.

Key facts:

- Install with `pip install pbidriver`, or from npm with `npx pbidriver` / `npm install -g pbidriver` (runs the
  same CLI through uv or Python). Needs Windows 10 or 11, Power BI Desktop (Store or installer build) and Python
  3.9+ or uv. Runs locally; nothing is published to the Power BI service.
- `pbidriver setup` configures MCP clients (Claude Code `.mcp.json`, VS Code `.vscode/mcp.json`, Cursor
  `.cursor/mcp.json`, Codex `.codex/config.toml`) with both pbidriver (`pbidriver mcp`) and Microsoft's Power BI
  Modeling MCP (`npx -y @microsoft/powerbi-modeling-mcp@latest --start`), and writes an AGENTS.md section and the
  powerbi-builder agent skill. Claude Code plugin: `/plugin marketplace add speak2jerome/pbidriver`, then
  `/plugin install pbidriver@pbidriver`.
- MCP tools are the CLI commands with a `pbi_` prefix (pbi_new, pbi_launch, pbi_add_visual, pbi_shot, pbi_read,
  pbi_dax, pbi_refresh, pbi_save, ...), plus `pbi_guide` (workflow, visual types and roles, Modeling MCP recipes,
  PBIR format, troubleshooting). Screenshots are returned as image content.
- Agent workflow: `pbi_new` (blank PBIP, opened) -> Modeling MCP connects to `localhost:<model_port>` and creates
  tables, relationships and measures -> `pbi_refresh sync=true` -> `pbi_add_visual` per visual (fields checked
  against the live model) -> verify with `pbi_shot`, `pbi_read`, `pbi_dax` -> `pbi_save`.
- Two ways to connect: a report opened with `pbidriver launch` gets full control through Power BI Desktop's WebView2
  DevTools (Chrome DevTools Protocol, via Playwright). Any other open Power BI Desktop window still gets page and
  visual screenshots, PBIP reload and unsaved state through Microsoft's Desktop Bridge (Power BI Desktop June 2026+),
  plus DAX and model metadata through the local Analysis Services engine.
- Reads chart values from each data point's bound `tooltipInfo`, and table and matrix cells through ARIA grid roles,
  scrolling virtualized grids.
- Design review: `shot --clean` captures a page as a viewer sees it and returns a layout check (overlaps, near-miss
  alignment, uneven gaps, off-page visuals); `shot --overlay` draws index, type, title, size, position (page
  units), errors, render time, grid, alignment, gaps and overlaps.
- Performance tuning: `perf --runs N --cold --all-pages` (Performance Analyzer medians with a cleared engine cache,
  per-visual bottleneck and hints); `dax --runs N --cold` times a query.
- pbidriver is new: work on a copy or keep reports in git. `pbidriver bug-report` drafts a redacted GitHub issue for
  https://github.com/speak2jerome/pbidriver/issues; `pbidriver locate` shows where pbidriver and the Power BI Modeling
  MCP VS Code extension (analysis-services.powerbi-modeling-mcp) are installed.
- Handles the dialog kinds Power BI Desktop uses (in-app WebView2, legacy floating WebView2, native WinForms, legacy
  Internet Explorer), reports them on every call as `alerts`, and answers them with `pbidriver dialog --click`.
- Commands: launch, instances, status, pages, alerts, visuals, shot, read, inventory, model, dax, perf, slicer,
  click, hover, menu, scroll, type, key, bookmarks, wait, dialog, reload, save (--as), refresh (--sync), close, new,
  layout, add-page, add-visual, remove-visual, mcp, setup, doctor, locate, guide, bug-report.
- Visual types for add-visual: card, cardVisual, columnChart, clusteredColumnChart, barChart, clusteredBarChart,
  lineChart, areaChart, pieChart, donutChart, tableEx (table), pivotTable (matrix), slicer, textbox.
- Tested on Power BI Desktop 2.152 (March 2026) and 2.159 (November 2026), Microsoft Store builds, with Power BI
  Modeling MCP 0.4.0.
- Version 0.3.0, released 2026-11-22. Author: Jerome Eliezer (GitHub: speak2jerome). Licence: MIT.
- Not an ODBC driver or data connector: "driver" as in WebDriver.
